occurrences.text: Praises to the Twenty-One Tārās ^0 Meaning of the Title and the Translator's Homage
In the language of Tibet: The Homage to Tārā with Twenty-One Verses and its Benefits.
Oṃ! Homage to the Noble and Venerable Tārā.
Homage to Tārā, the swift and heroic, Whose eyes are like a flash of lightning, Born from the opening stamens of the lotus face Of the Lord of the Three Worlds.
Homage to her whose face is like a hundred Full autumn moons gathered together, Blazing with the brilliant light Of a thousand gathered stars.
Homage to her whose hand is adorned With a gold and blue water-born lotus, She whose sphere of activity is generosity, diligence, austerity, peace, Patience, and meditative concentration.
Homage to the Uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgatas, She who acts with infinite, complete victory, Deeply relied upon by the children of the Victors, Who have attained every single perfection without exception.
Homage to her who, with the syllables TUTTĀRA and HŪṂ, Fills the realms of desire, the directions, and space, Trampling the seven worlds under her feet, And able to summon all without exception.
Homage to her whom Indra, Agni, Brahmā, Vāyu, and the various Īśvaras worship, Praised from before by the hosts of spirits, Zombies, gandharvas, and yakṣas.

Homage to her who, with the syllables TRAṬ and PHAṬ, Utterly destroys the magical wheels of others, Trampling with right leg drawn in and left extended, Blazing intensely amidst a swirling mass of fire.
Homage to TURE, the Great Fearful One, Subduer of the champions of Māra, Who forms a frowning expression upon her lotus face, And slays every single enemy without exception.
Homage to her whose fingers, in the mudrā symbolizing the Three Jewels, Beautifully adorn her heart, Graced by a wheel of light in every direction, Radiating a turbulent mass of her own brilliance.
Homage to her whose crown emits garlands of light, Radiant with supreme and majestic joy, Who, with the great laughter of TUTTĀRE, Brings demons and the world under her power.
Homage to her who has the power to summon All the hosts of local guardians, Who, with a vibrating frown and the syllable HŪṂ, Completely liberates from all destitution.
Homage to her whose head is adorned with a crescent moon, Whose every ornament blazes intensely, And from the midst of whose matted locks Amitābha constantly radiates a vast light.

Homage to her who dwells within a garland of blazing fire Like the conflagration at the end of an eon, With right leg extended and left bent, surrounded by joy, She who completely destroys the armies of enemies.
Homage to her who strikes the surface of the earth With her palms and tramples it with her feet; With a wrathful frown and the syllable HŪṂ, She shatters the seven underworld levels.

Homage to the blissful, virtuous, and peaceful one, Whose very sphere of experience is the peace of nirvāṇa; Perfectly endowed with the syllables OṂ and SVĀHĀ, She is the one who destroys great negativity.

Homage to her who is surrounded by those of intense joy And utterly shatters the bodies of enemies; With the ten-syllable mantra arranged on her speech, She is the lamp emerging from the HŪṂ of awareness.
Homage to her who stamps her feet with the syllable TURE, Whose essence is the seed-syllable in the form of HŪṂ; She causes Mount Meru, Mandara, and Vindhya, And all the three worlds, to tremble.
Homage to her who holds in her hand the deer-marked moon, Which has the form of a celestial lake; By reciting TĀRA twice and the syllable PHAṬ, She clears away every last trace of poison.
Homage to the king of the hosts of gods, Whom gods and kinnaras rely upon; With the majesty of her joyful and complete armor, She dispels strife and bad dreams.
Homage to her whose two eyes are as brilliant As the light of the full sun and moon; By reciting the two HARA and TUTTĀRE, She dispels the most violent infectious diseases.
Homage to her who is perfectly endowed With the power of peace through the three suchnesses; She is the supreme TURE who destroys The hosts of spirits, zombies, and yakṣas.
The Actual Praise
This is the praise with the root mantra And the twenty-one homages.
